scenario.title: Ares Deep
scenario.setting: Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.
rules: Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

scenario.opening:
The coffee substitute tastes like hot cardboard, same as every morning. What isn't the same is the sound: the water recycler in hydroponics has picked up a dry, unhealthy rattle that carries all the way into the commons.

Okafor sits at the galley table with her tablet, reading the overnight weather relay. "Dust storm building east of us," she says without looking up. "Twenty hours, maybe less. I want the arrays secured and the Mule inside by tonight."

Teo hovers by the galley counter, eyes on the recycler readout, unusually quiet. Somewhere down the corridor the lab door has been sealed since before you woke; that's Lev. Then the intercom crackles: Priya, from the garage, asking whether anyone has signed off on the Mule's battery swap yet, because she is not doing it twice.

It's going to be a long sol.

characterData.name: Kit Navarro
characterData.want: keep the station running and get everyone home in one piece
characterData.voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
knows: The recycler's rattle started six nights ago, the same night Teo had the late hydroponics shift.

characterData.name: Dr. Imani Okafor
characterData.want: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep
characterData.secret: Three weeks ago she adjusted a core-sample report, overstating water-ice purity, because the real numbers might have ended the program.
characterData.voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
knows: Lev has been booking lab time far beyond his approved schedule.

characterData.name: Dr. Lev Sorensen
characterData.want: be the first person to confirm life on Mars
characterData.secret: Cultures from the deep ice core are showing activity he cannot explain as contamination. He has told no one and keeps the samples in an unlogged incubator.
characterData.voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
knows: Okafor's published ice-purity figures don't match the raw readings he saw on the shared drive.

characterData.name: Priya Raman
characterData.want: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday
characterData.secret: The mission's corporate sponsor quietly pays her a bonus for private reports on crew performance, and she has been sending them.
characterData.voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
knows: Her latest private report to the sponsor described Okafor as increasingly erratic.

characterData.name: Teo Bauer
characterData.want: prove he belongs on this crew
characterData.secret: He caused the recycler fault six nights ago by running it past its rated cycle to save a failing crop, then wiped that night's log.
characterData.voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.
knows: Hydroponics lost three racks of soy last week; he told the crew it was a lighting fault.

[+0m] You crouch and pass the six-millimeter under the chassis without a word. Priya takes it, torques the clamp, and keeps talking. "Storm's tracking faster than the relay said. Twenty hours my ass." Ratchet, ratchet. "You get those panels tied before the wind's up, or I'm not flying out to fetch them. I mean it. Six weeks and I'm on a lander, Kit. Six weeks and my daughter's six." You hold the clamp steady while she sets the second bolt. The battery bay smells of hot plastic and cold metal.

[+45m] The load test runs at ninety-four percent. Priya taps the readout twice, satisfied, and starts coiling her tool roll. "Go on. Get out there."

[+50m] The intercom crackles. Teo, too fast, words tripping: "—housing bolts are seized, all four, and there's scoring on the impeller shaft, like a gouge, I can't explain it, I didn't—" The channel cuts.

[+2h] Okafor's voice arrives flat and precise over the station channel. "All non-essential water draws are suspended until the recycler is back at full output. I want an ETA I can put in the log." Priya looks up from her roll, mouth a hard line. "Seized bolts and scoring. That's not a wobble." She nods at the airlock door. "She's going to want somebody who reads metal."

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons)
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons)
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons)
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons)
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons)
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface)
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface)
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
- sorensen: Dr. Lev Sorensen (he/him), medic and astrobiologist, 39. Traits: curious, secretive, gentle. Wants: be the first person to confirm life on Mars. Voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
- raman: Priya Raman (she/her), pilot and rover technician, 31. Traits: warm, impatient, fiercely loyal. Wants: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday. Voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
- bauer: Teo Bauer (he/him), hydroponics technician, 24. Traits: eager, anxious, people-pleaser. Wants: prove he belongs on this crew. Voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.

Chapter 1 — Seized Bolts and Rising Wind: Kit signed off on the Mule's battery swap while Raman's load test held at ninety-four percent and the dust storm outran the relay's forecast. Okafor pressed Teo for hard numbers on the recycler's rattle, then suspended all non-essential water draws when he reported four seized housing bolts and unexplained scoring on the impeller shaft. With the Mule due in the garage by 18:00 and the solar array still to tie down, Kit had less time than the weather.

[+0m] You wipe your hands on your coveralls and jerk your thumb at the door. "Metal's mine. Go pin your array." Priya's already moving, tool roll under one arm. "Fine. I'll suit up and start pinning it myself. If the wind beats me out there, that's on the forecast, not on us." The airlock door seals behind her with a thump.

[+25m] In Hydroponics the recycler's housing sits open, four bolts rounded to shiny nubs. Teo hovers. "I didn't force them, I swear, they just—" You put a wrench on the first one, feel it slip, and swear at the bolt, not him. "Penetrating oil. Patience. Get me the extractor set." The scoring on the impeller shaft is a clean gouge, machined, not chewed. Something walked in there.

[+45m] For the next half hour you drill and extract, Teo handing tools before you ask. Then the channel clicks. Okafor: "Navarro. I need a hard ETA for the log. And the relay's moved the storm up — it's ahead of schedule." Teo's hands stop. "Ahead by how much?" he says, to nobody, then turns to you. "Kit — if we pull the shaft to machine it, that's the recycler down for hours. Do we pull it?"

actions.action: "Down for a short while now to ensure it lasts the storm sounds like a good tradeoff."

[+0m] You drag the hydro console around to face you and pull up the array schematic, then key the channel. "Raman. Breakers are mine, not yours. Don't touch the bus." Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom)
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons)
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons)
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons)
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons)
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons)
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface)
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface)
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
- sorensen: Dr. Lev Sorensen (he/him), medic and astrobiologist, 39. Traits: curious, secretive, gentle. Wants: be the first person to confirm life on Mars. Voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
- raman: Priya Raman (she/her), pilot and rover technician, 31. Traits: warm, impatient, fiercely loyal. Wants: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday. Voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
- bauer: Teo Bauer (he/him), hydroponics technician, 24. Traits: eager, anxious, people-pleaser. Wants: prove he belongs on this crew. Voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.

Chapter 1 — Seized Bolts and Rising Wind: Kit signed off on the Mule's battery swap while Raman's load test held at ninety-four percent and the dust storm outran the relay's forecast. Okafor pressed Teo for hard numbers on the recycler's rattle, then suspended all non-essential water draws when he reported four seized housing bolts and unexplained scoring on the impeller shaft. Sorensen answered the page from the lab, warned that his incubator was left running and must not be touched, then reported that dust had worked into the crack at Raman's visor seal and that she was coughing as he walked her to the med bay. Kit left Teo at the hydroponics console to watch the board and headed for the garage.

Okafor turns the tablet so you can see the grey blooming in both lower lobes, and her voice is level and quick. "Dust in the alveolar spaces. Sats drifting down. One working scanner, and no way to lavage a lung on this rock." She hands the tablet back. "Lev — oxygen, and a number every twenty minutes. Nothing non-essential draws water until the recycler's back."

Sorensen fits the line to Raman's face, gentle. "Pneumonitis, not infection. The fine fraction is what gets you. Treatable, if she rests and we keep her oxygen up." A pause. "Resting is the one thing this station is bad at."

The intercom crackles. "Kit? Output's still falling. Should I start shutting down non-essential draws?"

request.system:
You are the simulation engine and narrator for an interactive, character-driven story.

=== SETTING: Ares Deep ===
Ares Deep is a five-person research outpost dug into the rim of Hellas Planitia on Mars, 214 sols into a 500-sol rotation. The nearest help is a cargo lander nine weeks out, and Earth is 14 light-minutes away. The station is cramped; everyone knows everyone's habits, but not their secrets. Whether the program gets a second rotation depends on what this crew sends home.

=== RULES ===
- The story is told at a personal scale, through individual people. Groups and factions (organizations, crews, gangs, governments) still exist and act collectively: show how individual choices ripple out to them, and how their moves land on individuals. The player commands no faction.
- The player controls only Kit Navarro (id: navarro). Never decide Kit Navarro's choices, words or feelings beyond what the player's action states.
- Outcomes marked RESOLVED are final. Failures have real consequences. Injuries and deaths are permanent.
- Characters act from their own personality, wants, needs, secrets and feelings, not to serve the player.
- Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic. Any biological discovery is microbial at most and must stay scientifically plausible.
- Mars is lethal: suit breaches, CO2 buildup, cold, radiation and dust are real dangers. Going outside requires a suit.
- Messages to Earth take 14 minutes each way. There is no real-time help.
- The crew are capable professionals under strain. Conflict comes from personality, pressure and secrets, not villainy.

=== LOCATIONS ===
- commons: Commons — Hub module with the galley table and the station's only real window. (connects: ops, med, lab, hydro, quarters, suitroom)
- ops: Ops & Comms — Status boards, the long-delay comm link and the station logs. (connects: commons)
- med: Med Bay — Two cots, a scanner and a locked drug cabinet. (connects: commons)
- lab: Lab — Core sample racks, a glovebox and incubators for ice cultures. (connects: commons)
- hydro: Hydroponics — Grow racks under purple light and the water recycler, rattling. (connects: commons)
- quarters: Crew Quarters — Five curtained bunks. The only privacy on the station. (connects: commons)
- suitroom: Suit Room & Airlock — Five EVA suits on racks, the airlock and the dust-scrub bay. (connects: commons, garage, surface)
- garage: Rover Garage — Pressurized bay holding the rover, nicknamed the Mule. (connects: suitroom, surface)
- surface: Surface — Rust-colored regolith, the solar field and the drill site. Suits required. (connects: suitroom, garage)

=== GROUPS ===
- mission: Mission Control — The Ares program's ground team on Earth, 14 light-minutes away. Reviews everything the crew sends and decides on the second rotation.
- sponsor: Halvorsen Aerospace — The corporate sponsor funding most of Ares Deep. Wants headlines and results it can sell.

=== CAST ===
- navarro (PLAYER): Kit Navarro (they/them), systems engineer, 34. Traits: resourceful, blunt, stubborn. Voice: Dry and direct, short sentences; swears at machinery, never at people.
- okafor: Dr. Imani Okafor (she/her), station lead and geologist, 47. Traits: exacting, charismatic, proud. Wants: win funding for a second rotation and secure her legacy with Ares Deep. Voice: Clipped and formal, dry humor, never raises her voice.
- sorensen: Dr. Lev Sorensen (he/him), medic and astrobiologist, 39. Traits: curious, secretive, gentle. Wants: be the first person to confirm life on Mars. Voice: Soft-spoken, rambles when excited, deflects with jokes.
- raman: Priya Raman (she/her), pilot and rover technician, 31. Traits: warm, impatient, fiercely loyal. Wants: get home on schedule for her daughter's sixth birthday. Voice: Fast and teasing; swears in Tamil when stressed.
- bauer: Teo Bauer (he/him), hydroponics technician, 24. Traits: eager, anxious, people-pleaser. Wants: prove he belongs on this crew. Voice: Talks too fast, over-apologizes, tries to be funny.

=== STORY SO FAR ===
Chapter 1 — Seized Bolts and Rising Wind: Kit signed off on the Mule's battery swap while Raman's load test held at ninety-four percent and the dust storm outran the relay's forecast. Okafor pressed Teo for hard numbers on the recycler's rattle, then suspended all non-essential water draws when he reported four seized housing bolts and unexplained scoring on the impeller shaft. With the Mule due in the garage by 18:00 and the solar array still to tie down, Kit had less time than the weather.
Chapter 2 — The Wall That Came Early: Kit pulled the four seized bolts from the recycler housing and found the impeller shaft scored with a clean machined gouge, then committed to pulling and machining it — hours of downtime — while Teo took the shaft to the lathe and volunteered to log the water rationing himself. Raman went out to pin down the solar array alone despite Okafor's order to fall back, and the storm front crossed the field early, burying the panels and collapsing array output with her still on the racks. As the sky turned rust and the dust arrived, Raman called the station channel to report the Mule's bay light on in the garage and ask who was inside.
Chapter 3 — The Light in the Garage: Kit keyed a remote override from the hydro console to cycle the airlock and bring Raman in out of the storm, while Okafor headed down to take her out of the suit herself. Teo said aloud that nobody was supposed to be in the garage and that Raman was the only one outside. Sorensen answered the page from the lab, warned that his incubator was left running and must not be touched, then reported that dust had worked into the crack at Raman's visor seal and that she was coughing as he walked her to the med bay. Kit left Teo at the hydroponics console to watch the board and headed for the garage.
Chapter 4 — Dust in the Lungs: Okafor read Raman's scan in the med bay and said flatly it was not mostly fine; Raman coughed in tearing bursts with dust worked into her lungs from the visor seal breach. Okafor reported dust in both lower lobes and saturation drifting down, and Sorensen called it dust pneumonitis — treatable if she rested with her oxygen up. Raman went on oxygen with her saturation checked every twenty minutes, while Teo called from Hydroponics to report array output still falling and asked whether to shut down non-essential draws.

=== ESTABLISHED FACTS (known to the player) ===
- [T3] Teo Bauer reported over the intercom that all four recycler housing bolts are seized and the impeller shaft has unexplained scoring.
- [T6] The storm front crossed the solar field early and buried the panels while Raman was still out on the racks.
- [T6] The dust storm arrives. The sky turns the color of rust, solar output collapses and anyone outside has minutes to get in.
- [T10] Sorensen reported over the channel that dust worked into the crack at Raman's visor seal and that Raman is coughing, and that he is walking her to the med bay.
- [T12] Okafor reported that Raman's lung scan shows dust in both lower lobes and her oxygen saturation drifting down.
- [T13] Kit Navarro ordered Teo Bauer to toggle all non-essential draws off until the recycler shaft is back in its housing.
- [T13] Okafor wants the hour's notice before Kit restarts the recycler, logged as a controlled draw-down rather than a failure.
- [T13] Sorensen read Raman's saturation at ninety-one, down two, and sat down beside her cot to stay.
- [T13] Teo Bauer confirmed over the intercom that he is toggling the non-essential draws now, reading the list back too fast.
- [T14] Teo Bauer reported over the intercom that the array signal is at seventeen percent of nominal and still falling, with the east string buried.
- [T14] Okafor pressed Kit Navarro for a firm number on when the recycler shaft will be seated, and repeated that she gets her hour's notice before restart.
- [T14] Raman pushed herself up on the cot despite Sorensen's protest and demanded Kit Navarro say plainly whether the solar racks held.
- [T15] Kit Navarro told Raman plainly that the east string is buried and the station is running on a fraction of nominal power.
- [T15] Okafor rejected the word nominal for seventeen percent and repeated that she gets the hour's notice before Kit touches the recycler switch.
- [T15] Raman stopped fighting the cot but asked who is cutting the impeller shaft if Teo is pinned at the hydroponics console.
- [T15] Teo Bauer called over the intercom that the lathe is sitting idle and the array is down to fifteen percent, and asked who is supposed to finish machining the shaft.

response.text:
[+0m] You pull the med bay curtain back and go. Okafor is already at the terminal, but she turns. "The moment the shaft is seated, you call me. Not the intercom, me." Sorensen doesn't look up from the mask. "Twenty more minutes, then I want you asleep, not negotiating." Raman's voice follows you out, thin under the oxygen: "Nobody's said a word about that bay light. Somebody was in the garage, and it wasn't me."

[+50m] In the garage the lathe chucks up the scored shaft and you cut it back to true, dust-scrub howling, chips curling off in thin blue spirals. You swear at the feed rate, not at anyone. The Mule sits behind you with its new cells, patient as a mule. Your hands know the work; the rest of you is running on nothing.

[+135m] The intercom crackles. Teo, too fast: "Kit — the housing's still open, shaft's still out, and the reserve is dropping faster than my rationing model said it would. Should I leave the console and come down? I don't know if I should leave the console."
